mask.universal_step: Any LF byte forces a zero bit in the combined HI comparison; therefore a full-HI skip contains no LF.

intervals.skip_progress: t increases by16; prior skipped/prefix intervals contain no LF
intervals.fallback: Scalar comparison starts at t and precedes each increment; the first match is the global first LF.
intervals.chunk_progress: A found LF gives end=start+i+1, hence emitted<end<=length.
intervals.tail_cutpoint: A final-tail success exits on continuation bit before reusing stale R8.

write_protocol.sampled_pointer_values: B=load64(A+16),D=load64(A),V=load64(A+8), at the actual post-prologue load sites
write_protocol.indent_failure: Nonzero AL reaches0x157d25d before this piece flag store/payload request.
write_protocol.payload_failure: TEST0x157d087 flags survive MOVs/reloadedEAX to JNE0x157d09d, reaching AL1 after the pre-callback flag store.
write_protocol.success: All-success exit clears EAX at0x157d259; failed normal returns set AL1 only.
write_protocol.empty_input_or_empty_tail: No B-directed protocol access or callback; unchanged physical N additionally requires frame/alias separation.

conditions: Finite valid input bytes remain unchanged during this invocation, with no relevant range/address wrapping.
Normal callbacks preserve callee-save registers, protected frame/control slots and saved inputs.
The flag does not alias own frame/prologue/control writes, input bytes or later-needed metadata in a corrupting way.
D/V/B mean actual cached load values after the prologue; no pre-prologue memory-value assumption.
Method entries are fresh loads from cached V. Stable writer identity additionally needs method-slot preservation.
Final flag contents require callbacks to preserve the flag; otherwise only the ordered pre-callback store is qualified.
No physical output, private Rust layout/type/ABI, arbitrary alias safety or captured/emulated execution is claimed.

domain.entry_error: zero/nonzero raw byte, not a recovered bool type
domain.adapter: valid finite immutable input and stated frame/flag/alias conditions

conditions: Normal callback returns only; unwinding, faults, nonreturn and concurrent mutation excluded.
Observed memory must remain valid; state writes must not corrupt helper frame/control slots.
Callbacks preserve rbp/rbx/r12/r13/r14/r15, stack and saved value-argument slots.
Primitive destination facts use fresh loads; a same-writer specialization additionally requires formatter/method-slot and value-descriptor preservation.
Field-present byte0/1 is an explicit local domain, not an original Rust bool/layout claim.
Pretty value callbacks must preserve local A/L metadata for the known suffix adapter specialization; the shared N byte may be updated through the adapter protocol.
The shared N byte must be separated from adapter frame/prologue writes; physical preservation needs callback/alias conditions.
Arbitrary callback aliases/clobbers, physical output and nominal Rust types remain unqualified.
